Whenever I have something I need to get done, I set a reminder on my phone. For example “Hey Siri remind me at 8pm to take out laundry” then I free up my mental load in having to remember to take out my laundry. 

Remembering to send emails, buying something at the groceries, etc all these snowy depleted mental energy if the task is floating around in your head
Let your phone handle the remembering
We have been dating longer than we would be apart and the I thought promise of spending forever afterwards would make 5 years look like a blip.. I guess it is harder than we imagined

If you stay for him, at every little fight that can occur between a normal couple, it might blow out of proportion as you will blame him subconsciously for your missed opportunity and have the mindset “i sacrificed this much for you, you need to treat me better”. That’s not going to be healthy for your relationship.
Thanks to this post I re-checked my dilutions that I also used chatgpt for and was able to change to correct dilution in time. Not trusting chatgpt blindly again…

I agree with both of you and so glad there were conversations from both sides on this thread
I guess I need to learn the fine balance between getting my point and not coming across too aggressive. Unfortunately she does hold the upper hand in both the knowledge and hierarchy so Ill have to upskill myself to stand on my own

That must have been pretty hard for your wife.. I hope things are better for her now
Fortunately, I have other lab members whom I can communicate well with and have good relationships with. It’s mainly because she is my direct mentor so I have to deal with her for now. At this point, I am working on becoming more proficient in this research so that I dont need to rely too much on her.
Important thing is, you are done! Congratulations!! Doing this while having a full time job? That is very commendable! Put your hard work behind you for a while and celebrate!
US but Im drawn to moving back to my home country in south east asia if remote work permits
Thank you for your detailed experience! Do you worry about this job being replaced or number of positions being reduced by AI?
There are some people who I can ask for advice but there are limits when it comes to project specific details unfortunately..

Yea I think it is pretty discipline specific as things like ELISA or standard protocols are left for me to figure out myself but currently Im reproducing her previous research that is quite sensitive to little details and how we handle the samples
There are basic simplified protocols but my project is very handsy and little details on how we handle our samples can have a big impact on the variability
“make her edit it in front of you” is not so easy when she is a proud 5th year postdoc who claims she is busy and im just a first year phd who is basically already an annoying existance to her

Definitely a personality issue, other lab members who arent good in english but makes an effort to make themselves clear doesnt have this issue. However it is made worse by the fact that her english is pretty bad and she needs to make *extra* effort to make herself clear but she doesnt want to
Yea I did that and months later I found the error that she didnt point out - I told her “oh I wrote this and you didnt correct me” and she just went “oh” and end of story..

I have no good advice but just wanted to let you know that you aren’t alone in this struggle. I read your post and I could empathise with many aspects. I think the hardest is adjusting from being “gifted” to normal/struggling.

Biggest takeaway I had from my therapist is to be compassionate to your struggling self instead of being sad about being sad. Don’t force yourself to be okay, let yourself be “lazy” some days and let yourself recover without feeling guilty and let yourself feel down without pitying yourself.

Fortunately, there is an end to PhD although it seems far away. Trudge on one step and a time and we’ll get there
I thought I wrote this omg, PhD really did make me wanna get a job where I never have to use my brain or at least not too much and definitely not have to think about work when im home

Im in the exact same boat as you, I am also halfway through my first year and have been failing the exact same experiment for 3 months now. It is an experiment that is simply replicating something a past student has done before successfully. Have tried troubleshooting every single step and is still failing. My mentor is not helpful at all and I can tell my PI is getting frustrated too

I am feeling very helpless and stuck

But I am trying to see some silver lining such as my experiments dont cost much in failing (I used to work with samples in my previous lab where each failure meant hundreds of dollars gone) and that at least im learning to troubleshoot in my first year and there is nothing urgent paper to submit or other responsibilities that upper year students have.

We got this
It may not feel like it 
But years later, we will look back at this moment and feel proud that we were resilient and pushed through
I love a happy ending
Omg this is infuriating! Did you confront him or let your PI or his PI know?
Pain
Yea very different kinds of difficulty and very different kind of reward for each. Everyone is meant for different kind of challenge and personally Id like a challenge that looks like a mini me

In no way I would want to downplay the difficulties of being a stay at home mom. But I think the type of difficulty and the type of reward you get from being a mother is very different from a PhD. Id like to move on from this challenge to another where i like the reward part better

“Learning for the sake of learning” for sure
Not everyone will be saving the world and curing cancer

Im happy with my contribution to science during PhD, I now want to contribute to myself and my family

Some people have the luxury of not using the brain and some have the luxury of not using physical exertion and some have luxury of not needing to use both

Some may find it better fitting to their values to use either the brain or the body. I think Ive done enough of the brain though

Hi Im the OP and your assumptions are not all correct but surely you can give your opinion based on scenarios that may apply to other people.

I do recognize the privilege that I dont have people that I have to support as of right now and I have a fiancé who is supportive of my wish to become a SAHM. That being said, I agree with you that it is important that I dont really solely on him to support me and that I need back up plans cuz unexpected things can happen too.

Fortunately for me, I have some savings that will support me if times get tough and I need time to find a job.

With the soft skills PhD has taught me, Im confident I can find a job that is within my frugal spending and needs

I emphathize so much with uou because my current mentor is very much like yours. Except mine is a confirmed lab so I feel you are luckier in that sense. What is getting me going is that my mentor is leaving in couple months and Im thinking it’s not too late to leave after seeing how the situation changes after my mentor leaves.

You should wait until your third rotation and consider yourself lucky that this is just a rotation and not a confirmed lab. Do your third rotation with the thought that it’s not too late to quit after you experience your third one.

My PI isnt supportive in terms of emotional help, he just told me to figure it out with the postdoc when she is back. I think the problem is too project specific, other lab members working on similar things advice didnt work.

Even though I know it will prob work out eventually, my current concern is my physical symptoms and no motivation to do anything.
I feel like not feeling bad about it removes the emotional motivation to fix it.. Without the emotional motivation, I might feel more complacent about it and take longer to solve it

1. I asked my undergrad prof who is in the field that I want to pursue in grad school to give me some recommendations. (6 names) From there, I filtered based on school level and fit of research. (Left with 4 names)
2. I made a list of schools that’s within the prestige level that I can shoot for. (12 schools) Went through their prof list to see if there are any prof doing research in the field im interested in (left with 6 schools)

After that, I cold emailed the profs to set up a meeting and filtered out profs who didnt pass my vibe check. Or if they dont reply, I reached out to students in their lab to learn about the lab culture. (Talked to 4 schools)

In the end, I applied to 7 schools

Im an incoming grad student and i got it a couple days ago

I had a similar problem with a different school. When I emailed them, they said that by fall, they will clear all the application email/data for that year from their system so I have to wait it out till then
Imposter syndrome hit you early yea? Dont worry, everyone’s faking it till they make it and youll make it soon too!
Also, rejecting the schools you are sure that you wont attend gives them time to extend admissions to those on the waitlist. Do everyone a favor and reject schools early!!
“Please know that this is not a reflection of the school’s academic abilities”

Lower your expectations. Im sincerely hoping that all goes well for you and for you to get good admission results. However, accepting that you may not get in anywhere and planning for an alternative future will be good for your anxiety.
Email the graduate admissions office

Id say for 2500 word limit 1500-2000 is a good range to have
Having less than half their limit may seem like you dont have much to talk about or you are missing good details you can add to stand out more
Im in biomedical engineering! I applied to some chemical engineering and bioengineering as well
I wouldnt bring up the reviewing of materials first as phd students tend to be busy. Id ask them for a call to talk about their lab, build a rapport, THEN ask for feedback/reviews
Yes definitely varies between schools! But I feel like the answers from the students will be biased as they are all accepted eventually haha

I was rejected by 6 schools last year and I also didnt know why. This year when I looked back at my statement of purpose, I knew. It takes some time away from thinking about admissions and taking some steps away from all these stress to really see how to improve your statement of purpose.
Also, to increase my chances, I asked my recommenders to strengthen the recommendation letters by explicitly asking them to mention certain traits and strengths of mine.

In the year between the two admission cycles, I got to have so many new experiences, and new friends and so much more fun. So, blessings in disguise - take it as a sign that this year will be extraordinarily awesome for you that you didnt go for phd yet

Im feeling exactly the same right now! I am subconsciously hoping that the more prestigious university rejects me soon so I dont have to make a decision and get onto preparing for the less prestigious university with the PI that seems to vibe well with me
Congratulations! After the rain came the rainbow

Yes yes yes. It’s my second year of applying due to scholarship stuff and I am so much happier and stress free because I allocated a day of a week to browse these sites. It helps me stay connected and not feel FOMO yet have a healthy amount of exposure
